paragraphs.text: Neural circuits must represent quantities such as location and eye position while individual spikes fluctuate. paragraphs.text: The guide assumes undergraduate calculus, basic probability, and linear algebra. Neuroscience terms and the required stochastic-process, information, filtering, and random-field ideas are taught where needed. The first chapter establishes spikes, population activity, fixed points, covariance, and diffusion. Chapters 2 and 3 derive the persistent-activity model and its information bound. Chapter 4 applies the dynamical ideas to eye drift. Chapter 5 develops spatial Gaussian processes and place-field geometry. Chapter 6 brings the results together and compares related work.
